To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

four non-truncation mutations of the SLC6AG8 gene responsible for the Cr transporter deficiency syndrome were characterized for their electrogenic activity and Cr transport in the oocyte expression system and in patient's fibroblast.

the four non-truncation mutations of the human creatine transporter (hCT) SLC6A 8, identified in patients presenting various clinical severity, led to the complete inhibition of electrogenic and transport activity.
four mutations of the SLC6AG8 gene, encoding the creatine transporter (CrT), led to the complete inhibition of CrT electrogenic activity and Cr uptake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional and electrophysiology characterization of four non truncating mutations in SLC6A 8 responsible for creatine (Cr ) transporter deficiency syndrome.
the characterization of the pathogenic mechanisms of SLC6AC8 mutations.
a novel and original approach to the characterization of the functional properties of SLC6 A8 and its mutations.

the loss of electrogenic activity is the common feature of the non-truncating SLC6 A8 mutations.

the loss of electrogenic activity is a key factor in the pathophysiology of SLC6a8 deficiency syndrome.
